intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene (615618) on chromosome 3q13.33.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the POGLUT1 gene.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy-21 (LGMDR21) is a muscular dystrophy with slowly progressive proximal weakness that mainly affects the lower limbs. Onset is usually in adulthood, but congenital and infantile onset have been reported. Muscle imaging shows a distinctive 'inside-to-outside' pattern of fatty degeneration in the thigh muscles. Muscle biopsy shows hypoglycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan and reduced numbers of satellite cells (Servián-Morilla et al., 2020).

checks.evidence_quote: The weakness showed a proximal distribution, with a clear predominance in the lower limbs and slow progression.

checks.claim: The weakness in LGMDR21 mainly affects the lower limbs.
checks.evidence_quote: The weakness showed a proximal distribution, with a clear predominance in the lower limbs and slow progression.

checks.evidence_quote: The muscle imaging pattern resembled an “inside-to-outside” fatty degeneration because the most affected segment was the inner region of each muscle in the anterior and posterior compartment of the thigh.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reported 15 patients with LGMDR21 from 9 unrelated families. The families came from Spain, Bulgaria, Italy, Germany, the USA, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, and 4 of them were consanguineous. Onset was congenital in 1 patient, infantile (before age 3 years) in 2 and adult in 12. Weakness was proximal, predominated in the lower limbs and progressed slowly. Seven patients whose disease began in their teens needed a wheelchair between the third and fifth decades. Eleven patients had mild to moderate scapular winging. Six patients developed mild to severe respiratory involvement from their mid-forties onward, regardless of age at onset, and 2 of them used ventilatory support at night. There were no significant bulbar, cardiac or other systemic manifestations. Serum CK was normal in most patients. The authors noted this as a diagnostic clue that distinguishes LGMDR21 from most other recessive LGMDs.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) described a 24-year-old man with congenital-onset disease (family 2, patient II.1). He presented with hypotonia and developed proximal lower limb weakness after learning to walk. He later developed weakness, wasting and contractures of the upper limbs. He also had mild facial weakness, ptosis, nasal voice, elbow contractures, myopathic facies and an arched palate. He had used a wheelchair since age 22. His disease progressed faster and was more severe than in the adult-onset cases.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) reviewed lower limb muscle MRI or CT in 11 of the 15 patients. All 11 showed an 'inside-to-outside' pattern of fatty degeneration. The first muscles affected were the inner segments of the vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and vastus intermedius, the posterior thigh compartment and the gastrocnemius. Lower leg muscles were better preserved than thigh muscles. The pattern was clearest early in the disease but could still be seen in the vastus lateralis at end stage.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) studied 15 patients with LGMDR21 from 9 families. Using next-generation sequencing (gene panels or whole-exome sequencing) with Sanger confirmation, they identified 9 missense mutations and 1 nonsense mutation in the POGLUT1 gene, in the homozygous or compound heterozygous state. In every family the mutations segregated with disease, and no asymptomatic carriers were found. The novel variants were either absent from ExAC or present in the heterozygous state in no more than 2 of more than 60,000 non-Finnish European controls.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) used several assays to test the mutations. In HEK293T cells, several mutant proteins (I129T, R98W, W308L and C102F) were secreted poorly. These mutants gave little or no rescue of Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells. Other mutant proteins (Y57C and R183W) were secreted normally but had markedly reduced enzymatic activity. In a Drosophila myogenesis rescue assay, all of the variants tested reduced the myogenic activity of POGLUT1.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found reduced levels of the NOTCH1 intracellular domain (NICD) in patient muscle. The number of PAX7-positive satellite cells was significantly reduced (5 patients vs 5 controls). Patient muscle had no or very few eMHC-positive regenerating fibers, whereas disease controls had many. The authors suggested that reduced Notch1 signaling disturbs satellite cell biology and causes the dystrophy. They proposed that alpha-dystroglycan hypoglycosylation contributes as a secondary defect.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) cultured primary myoblasts from the compound heterozygous D233E/R279Q patient. Compared with control cells, these myoblasts proliferated less and had fewer proliferating and self-renewing (PAX7+) cells. They also had more differentiating cells, with increased myogenin expression and a higher fusion index. The authors concluded that slow proliferation and facilitated myogenic differentiation underlie POGLUT1-related muscular dystrophy.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) tested patient variants in a Drosophila myogenesis rescue assay using rumi(79/79) flies. Wildtype human POGLUT1 fully rescued the shortened indirect flight muscles. The D233E, R183W, I129T and Y57C mutants were expressed at normal levels but gave only partial rescue, and the C102F mutant gave no rescue. The authors concluded that all of the variants tested reduce the myogenic activity of POGLUT1.

paragraphs.text: Servián-Morilla et al. (2020) found a homozygous ile129-to-thr (I129T) mutation in the POGLUT1 gene in a man with infantile-onset LGMDR21 (family 3). The mutation was absent from ExAC. In HEK293T cells, the mutant protein was secreted poorly and was not detected in cell lysates, suggesting severe destabilization. It did not rescue Notch1 EGF1-18 secretion in POGLUT1-knockout cells. In Drosophila, the mutant was expressed normally but only partially rescued myogenesis.
